summary: Phase 1 (Pre-Visit Briefing Agent) frontend testing. Executed all 12 requested flows end-to-end against the live preview URL as doctor (dr.layla@sihha.ai) and patient (omar.patient@sihha.ai). Ran /app/backend/seed_phase1.py first because the environment was empty (no encounters, no shared patients) — after seeding, all flows worked. Result: doctor sidebar has nav-doctor + nav-doctor-schedule; schedule page lists seeded encounters with correct 'Not generated' badges and patient names (Omar Farouk, Noura Aziz, Sami Rahman); patient dropdown populated from /doctor/patients; encounter row navigates to encounter-detail-page; briefing-empty-state → generate-briefing-btn shows briefing-skeleton with 'Reviewing 90 days of patient data…', LLM completes in ~30-45s; ai-draft-banner + all 6 briefing sections (headline, concerns, vitals, medications, discussion, gaps, interactions) render for Omar; inline headline PATCH is debounced and persists across reload; followup-panel shows the 'Answers come from this patient's data only.' subtitle and 3 starter questions; in-scope BP question returns assistant reply with 3 citation chips; out-of-scope 'What should I prescribe' correctly renders followup-refusal block (no error toast); Review & Sign accepts the confirm dialog and swaps in signature-line with doctor name + timestamp, hiding sign/regenerate buttons; follow-up panel still functional after signing. Patient omar.patient does NOT see nav-doctor / nav-doctor-schedule, direct visit to /doctor/schedule shows schedule-access-denied, and /doctor/encounters/<id> shows encounter-access-denied. Regression: patient dashboard, /chat, /pill-id all load cleanly.

integration_issues.issue: When a citation's collection is 'clinical_artifacts' (which happens for the LLM's own self-referencing briefing chip — first chip in the Omar BP answer was 'clinical_artifacts · Briefing chief concern: frequent BP readings above recorded normal ranges'), scrollToCite() finds no matching #cite-clinical_artifacts-* nor #sect-clinical_artifacts element and silently falls back to toast.info('That record is not shown in this briefing'). No terracotta ring is applied. Vitals / medications / alerts chips work correctly (matching #sect-vitals, #sect-medications, #sect-alerts exist). Consider either (a) filtering clinical_artifacts-collection citations out of chips, or (b) mapping them to #sect-briefing so the doctor sees a highlight instead of a muted toast.

issues: Row status column shows 'SCHEDULED' next to the briefing badge; visually it can be mistaken for a second badge because the two chips sit side-by-side in the same visual rhythm. Consider deemphasising the encounter.status label (e.g., moving it to the left column under the time) so 'NOT GENERATED / DRAFT / SIGNED' is the dominant tag.

seed_phase1.py schedules encounters at now + rand(0..30)*day but then most rows visible on the schedule are dated 'Aug 17-27, 2026' — several days in the *past* relative to today (~Aug 18, 2026 in the test env). The list is sorted by scheduled_at desc so past encounters push future ones off-screen. Not a Phase 1 bug per se, but a demo-data issue that hurts the first impression of the schedule page.

action_items: Consider mapping clinical_artifacts citations to #sect-briefing in scrollToCite() so the first citation chip on every AI answer produces a visible highlight instead of a muted 'That record is not shown in this briefing' toast (or filter these self-references out of the chip list on the backend side in briefing_qa.py).
Optional: adjust seed_phase1.py to schedule encounters strictly in the future (e.g., now + 1..30 days) so the seeded demo data on /doctor/schedule doesn't look stale immediately after seeding.
critical_code_review_comments: EncounterDetail.jsx queueSave uses an 800ms debounce which is under the 2s described in the request — works fine but the review request specifies 'wait ~2s for the debounced PATCH'; the code is actually 800ms so persistence is faster than the spec but consistent (no bug).
DoctorSchedule.jsx: 'reviewed' and 'draft' both map to the same 'Draft' label. Fine for now, but if you later add an intermediate 'reviewed but unsigned' state it will collide with plain draft.

FollowUpPanel.jsx: assistant messages without citations render a red 'No citations — unverified' warning; the refusal block bypasses this because refusal messages are matched first via `m.refused`. Verified in test — refusal renders the correct out-of-scope block, not the unverified warning.
test_credentials: dr.layla@sihha.ai / Doctor@123 (doctor); omar.patient@sihha.ai / Patient@123 (patient). /app/memory/test_credentials.md is present and correct.
seed_data_creation: Ran /app/backend/seed_phase1.py to (re)create dr.layla, omar/noura/sami patients, 90 days of vitals/meds/dose_logs per patient, and 5 encounters. Also created one extra 'TEST_regression checkup' encounter for Omar on 2026-03-01 via the new-encounter form — schedule reload race made my playwright count check flaky, but the encounter did POST successfully (no error toast, no 4xx/5xx in backend log). One briefing was generated and signed for enc_1a4e941c523b (Omar) — DO NOT reuse that encounter for edit tests since it is now read-only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 frontend passes. If you re-run: (1) the environment starts empty — always run `cd /app/backend && python seed_phase1.py` first (the script takes ~90s and inserts ~558 vitals + 540 dose_logs across 3 patients). (2) After my run, encounter enc_1a4e941c523b (Omar) has a SIGNED briefing headlined 'TEST_EDIT_178964' — pick a different 'NOT GENERATED' Omar row for regenerate/edit tests. (3) Auth uses httpOnly cookies (login redirects to /dashboard for doctor role too — sidebar toggle to Doctor Portal via nav-doctor works). (4) LLM briefing generation takes 30-45s and QA questions 15-30s — use 90s timeouts. (5) There are three encounter rows per seeded patient because the seed loops 5 encounters * multiple runs; not a bug from Phase 1 code but worth knowing.
rca of the issue: Only functional gap found is the citation-chip → section-scroll fallback for collection='clinical_artifacts'. RCA: the QA agent (briefing_qa.py) returns cited_records with collection='clinical_artifacts' for citations that reference the briefing itself; the frontend scrollToCite() only knows about #cite-<collection>-<id> and #sect-<collection> where <collection> ∈ {vitals, medications, alerts, interactions}. There is no #sect-clinical_artifacts / #sect-briefing target, so the chip silently no-ops (toast.info). Fix: either add id='sect-briefing' to the headline card (id already exists!) and change the fallback in scrollToCite to try #sect-briefing when collection === 'clinical_artifacts', or filter self-references out on the backend.
